strong-emotional-certainty-intention.context: Neutral, but can sound formal in casual settings. Use with discretion.
strong-emotional-certainty-intention.notes: Use when expressing a strong intention or plan, but not when asking if someone else has plans. Do not use with questions or with conjectural form.
strong-emotional-certainty-intention.nuance: Stresses strong intention or conviction, but can sound overconfident or arrogant if not used properly.

examples.japanese: 8月に友達と一緒に大阪へ行くつもりです
examples.english: I plan to go to Osaka with my friends in August.

examples.japanese: 今年私の母国へ帰らないつもりです
examples.english: I am planning not to return to my homeland this year.

strong-emotional-certainty-intention.context: Polite and formal, but also found in everyday conversation when explaining reasons.
strong-emotional-certainty-intention.notes: When stating a purpose, follow with 辞書形; when explaining cause, use it with a past tense verb/negative form. Confusing the purpose and reason forms of 〜ために, and misuse with casual conversational structures.
strong-emotional-certainty-intention.nuance: ~ために often implies a level of intention and planning, whereas in its causative form it denotes an inevitable causative relation.

examples.japanese: 就職のために、毎日プログラミングを練習しています
examples.english: I am practicing programming every day for employment.

examples.japanese: 日本語を話すために、日本に来た
examples.english: I came to Japan to speak Japanese

strong-emotional-certainty-intention.meaning: when it comes to ___, ___　(focus on ability and higher than others)
strong-emotional-certainty-intention.context: Formal and casual, but somewhat assertive, often used in debates, arguments, or playful competitions.
strong-emotional-certainty-intention.notes: Use 〜にかけては after a subject or topic, to express its superiority or excellence in the following context. Often mistakenly used to compare two equal topics instead of emphasizing the superiority of one.
strong-emotional-certainty-intention.nuance: 〜にかけては underlines a speaker's emphasis or slightly competitive sense of superiority on a certain topic or ability.

examples.japanese: かんさんは人を笑わせることにかけては、クラスで一番だ。
examples.english: When it comes to making people laugh, Kansan is the best in the class.
